lead_headline: Restaurant tracker adds 4 new leads (2 openings, 2 closures/temp closures)—active pipeline holds at 92 cases—while foreclosure filings surge 37% and subscriber net flatlines at zero for second straight day

restaurant.blurb: 4 new leads today (2 openings, 2 closures) hold active count at 92 (47 openings, 45 closures)—Wednesday additions include Wapos Cantina opening Mexican outpost in Rosedale's former El Tepehuan space (confidence 9) and Mendocino Farms launching third Denver sandwich shop at Union Station (confidence 9). Closures: Powered By Besitos food truck shutters West Colfax operations (confidence 9), New Dragon Chinese restaurant marks 13-year Berkeley run with temp closure (confidence 7). Today's 4-case intake matches Monday's pace but trails weekend burst—April's 8-day run posts 92 active leads split 51% openings versus 49% closures, tightening from Monday's 52/48 spread as closure velocity accelerates. Union Station corridor notches fifth opening in 11 days as Mendocino Farms joins C Burger, Ogo Korean BBQ, High Point, G-Que BBQ downtown cluster.

foreclosure.blurb: 48 filings this week hold 37% above last week's 35-case floor with Douglas County's $1.1M Beebalm Loop property anchoring zero $2M+ filings—total week value slides to $15.2M from prior period's $18M+ as 115 auctions queue for next seven days.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications today extend statewide freeze to 39 consecutive days—Wednesday marks ninth straight zero-filing session as April's first eight days post 0/9 shutout, now 225% beyond December 2024's 12-day record drought. System blackout enters sixth week with no Liquor Enforcement Division updates, no legislative signals, no industry association communications—estimated backlog climbs to 85-115 applications as void spans all Colorado counties (Denver, Arapahoe, Douglas, El Paso, Boulder, Larimer, Weld, Broomfield), all license types (retail, tavern, hotel/restaurant, brew pub, distillery, winery), all categories (new, renewal, transfer, modification). Database holds 13,731 historical entries but registers zero March 1–April 8 activity, obliterating January-February's 15-20 weekly baseline and all seasonal filing patterns.

reputation.blurb: 1 mention today drags week to 53 citations (−16% vs prior week's 63) across 15 sources—Wednesday's lone pickup: Instagram's Whataburger south metro teaser. Week's leaders shift: Instagram (16 mentions), Denver Post (11), Facebook (8), with social platforms claiming 45% share versus prior week's 40% traditional/social split. Source count holds at 15 outlets (down from prior period's 16) while daily mention rate tumbles to 7.6/day from last week's 9.0/day, confirming April's downward trajectory after March's sustained 10+/day baseline. Notable gap: zero Hoodline, X.com pickups Tuesday-Wednesday after combined 5 mentions Monday.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +0 yesterday (0 new, 0 canceled) marks second consecutive flatline day as MTD holds −1 (−0.1/day through 8 days) while 90-day net maintains +137. Tuesday's zero activity mirrors Monday's stall—past week delivers −1 net (8 new, 9 canceled) versus prior week's +19 (31 new, 12 canceled), marking 105% net reversal as acquisition collapses 74% while cancellations slide 25%. Eight-day April start posts −1 net (15 new, 16 canceled, −0.1/day) versus March's opening stretch (+29 net, +4.1/day), confirming 102% momentum flip. Recent fortnight splits sharply: March 25-31 surged +18 net (28 new, 10 canceled, +2.6/day), April 1-8 stumbled −19 net (15 new, 34 canceled, −2.4/day)—new subscriber intake cratered 46% while cancellations tripled, inverting March's +2.6/day pace to April's −2.4/day drag. YTD +130 (+1.3/day) cushions monthly bleed but current trajectory projects −4 April finish unless 33-subscriber swing materializes.
